prose:
alphaXiv presents OpenAI's matrix-multiplication manuscript with an abstract claiming exponent nine fourths over every field and an explicitly labeled AI-generated overview. That overview explains a contradiction argument involving tensor-network compression and list-distinctness lower bounds, while keeping circuit cost separate from hardware runtime.

This is another presentation of [the same preprint](../summaries/8b1e8b2640d9.md), not independent mathematical confirmation. An AI overview is a guide to the manuscript rather than expert certification; neither it nor its citation markers prove the argument correct. Exponent equality is not automatically a fixed-constant Theta(n^2.25) implementation, and no proof checker, algorithm or benchmark was run here.
highlights: Abstract repeats the same exponent claim
No experiment or hardware speedup is established
AI citation markers are not proof certification
Same manuscript is not independent corroboration
